diagnosis.explanation: All three fitted runs went digging through the packaged plugin source and then cloned the clock plugin under a new id. The map line 'Only to change a widget's code: run omarchy plugin clone...' presents cloning as a normal path, so the agents treated it as one, while vanilla simply edited the format option on the existing shell.json entry.
Same failure on the Opus run. It read the widget's timer/format code, decided a clone was warranted, and renamed the bar entry, so the stock widget id no longer has the requested option.
Same failure on the Haiku run. The shell-guide trigger only fires on before:edit, so it was injected after the clone had already happened through bash; the map's clone wording drove the choice.

edits.old:
- Built-in widget options (format etc.): edit its existing entry in `shell.json` `bar.layout` and keep its id.
- Only to change a widget's code: run `omarchy plugin clone omarchy.<name>`, then edit `.config/omarchy/plugins/<username>.<name>/`. Cloning switches the bar to the clone. Never edit the packaged copy.
edits.new:
- Built-in widget options (format etc.): edit its existing entry in `shell.json` `bar.layout` and keep its stock id. That is the whole change; don't inspect or second-guess plugin internals.
- Clone (`omarchy plugin clone omarchy.<name>` → `.config/omarchy/plugins/<username>.<name>/`) only when the user explicitly asks to change widget code. Cloning replaces the stock id in the bar. Never edit the packaged copy.

edits.note: Read /usr/share/omarchy/default/agents/skills/omarchy/plugins.md first. Bar is omarchy-shell, not Waybar; idle values are seconds. Widget display/format changes go on the existing shell.json bar.layout entry, keeping its stock id. Clone only if the user explicitly asks to change widget code; never edit packaged ones.

proposal.expected_effect: Agents will set widget options directly on the stock shell.json entry instead of cloning plugins, which matches the vanilla behavior that passed, and the clone path stays available for explicit code-change requests.
